about.title: Lathrop Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Lathrop's growth along I-5 and Harlan Road has brought new retail centers, distribution warehouses, and apartment communities — and with them, the everyday hazards that cause falls: wet entryways, uneven parking lots, poor lighting, and cluttered aisles. When a fall happens on someone else's property, California law asks whether the property owner or manager knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to fix or warn about it. That question often comes down to details: how long a spill sat before you fell, whether a mat was missing, or what a surveillance camera captured. San Joaquin County property owners and their insurers frequently push back on these claims, arguing the hazard was open and obvious or that it appeared moments before the fall. An independent attorney can help gather the evidence — photos, incident reports, witness statements, and video — before it disappears. LawProactive connects you with that attorney for free, and there's no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Settling

items.title: Proving the Property Owner Knew or Should Have Known
items.desc: California premises cases hinge on notice — showing the hazard existed long enough that a reasonable owner would have caught and fixed it. An attorney knows how to dig up maintenance logs, prior complaints, and inspection records to establish this.

items.title: Preserving Surveillance Footage Before It's Erased
items.desc: Many Lathrop retailers and apartment complexes overwrite security video within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request and preserve footage can be the difference between a strong claim and one with no evidence.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly distracted or not looking down, you can still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help make sure a partial-fault argument doesn't unfairly wipe out your claim.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Lathrop?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit against a private property owner. If the fall happened on government property, such as a city sidewalk or public building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim filing. Because Lathrop has a mix of private retail and public infrastructure along corridors like Harlan Road and SR-120, it's worth having an attorney confirm which deadline applies to your situation quickly.

items.question: What if I fell at a warehouse or distribution center near I-5?
items.answer: Lathrop's location along I-5 has brought in numerous warehouse and logistics facilities, and falls there can involve pallets, forklift traffic, or spilled materials rather than typical retail hazards. These cases often involve additional layers, such as contractors or third-party maintenance companies, which can affect who is responsible. An attorney can help sort out which party or parties may be liable.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive's connection service is free, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you receive a settlement or award. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward after speaking with an attorney.
